microsoft_purview_copilot.summary: Copilot and AI app interactions are logged automatically in Audit (Standard) if auditing is enabled. Fields: Operation=CopilotInteraction (admin ops e.g. UpdateTenantSettings, CreatePlugin), RecordType (CopilotInteraction, ConnectedAIAppInteraction, AIAppInteraction, TeamCopilotInteraction), Workload (Copilot, ConnectedAIApp, AIApp), AppIdentity (e.g. Copilot.MicrosoftCopilot.BizChat, Copilot.Studio.<guid>, ConnectedAIApp.Entra.AppId, AIApp.SaaS.AppName), AppHost, AccessedResources (id, SiteUrl, SensitivityLabelId, action), Messages (message ids, isPrompt, JailbreakDetected), AISystemPlugin (BingWebSearch = web grounding), AgentId/Name/Version, ModelTransparencyDetails (provider/name; model name not available for M365 Copilot), ClientRegion, DLP deferral bitmask. Third-party AI app records (AIAppInteraction, some ConnectedAIAppInteraction) are pay-as-you-go with 180-day retention and need enabling; AIApp records come from network/browser DLP. Search via Purview portal > Audit by operation/recordType/workload; AppIdentity filtering must be done offline after export. Records reference prompt/response by message id; the doc does not say the prompt text is in the audit record itself (content via other Purview features: unverified).

google_workspace_gemini.summary: Admin console > Reporting > Audit and investigation > 'Gemini for Workspace log events' (needs Audit & Investigation privilege). Events: Feature Utilization; attributes Action (e.g. GENERATE_IMAGES, GENERATE_SLIDES, SUMMARIZE_THREAD), Actor email, Application name, Event Category (active_conversations, active_generate, active_summarize, active_unspecified, inactive, unknown), Agent info and By-an-agent flag, Feature Source, IP ASN, User device ID. Default view last 7 days; retention period not stated on that page (see separate 'data retention and lag times' page: unknown). Page does not say prompts/responses are logged. Separate audit logs for Gemini Notebook (announced Sept 3, 2026) viewable in security investigation tool and exportable to BigQuery (export off until enabled).

chatgpt_enterprise_compliance_api.summary: OpenAI Compliance Platform/API for Enterprise and Edu: logs and metadata of ChatGPT workspace usable for eDiscovery/DLP/SIEM; two patterns (immutable append-only audit log stream; stateful API). Logs Platform retention only 30 days, so customers must pull and archive continuously. Deleted data not recoverable. Exact data types (conversation content, files, GPTs) and API paths: unknown (help page returned 403; claims come from search-result summary).
chatgpt_enterprise_compliance_api.confidence: unverified (search summary of official help article)

claude_enterprise_compliance_api.summary: Base https://api.anthropic.com/v1/compliance/*, header x-api-key plus anthropic-version. GET /v1/compliance/activities (Activity Feed: id, created_at, actor{email,user_id,ip_address,user_agent}, type e.g. claude_chat_created). Key types: Compliance Access Key (claude.ai; all endpoints) and Admin API key (Console; Activity Feed only, scope read:compliance_activities). Enterprise-only endpoints retrieve/delete chats, files, projects and retrieve session transcripts for Cowork, Claude Code, Claude Science, Claude for Microsoft 365, Docs/Sheets/Slides add-ins and Claude in Chrome (local sessions captured only while signed in with the Enterprise account). Rate limit 600 req/min per parent org. Separate: audit log CSV export in claude.ai admin settings (narrow, capped lookback), Analytics APIs (aggregates), OpenTelemetry logging (can capture prompts), inference hooks (inline deny). Standalone Console orgs: activity feed only; one third-party article states the feed does not log inference content (third-party, treat cautiously). Retention of transcripts: unknown.

5_korea_considerations.note: Not legal advice; statute text could not be fully fetched (law.go.kr returned titles only). Bullets 1-4 are unverified background to be checked against 국가법령정보센터 (law.go.kr) and 대법원 종합법률정보 (glaw.scourt.go.kr) before use.

bullets.text: Art. 3 prohibits interception (감청) outside statutory procedure and Art. 4 bars use of evidence obtained by unlawful interception; real-time capture of an employee's in-flight messages/prompts (e.g. TLS-inspecting proxy reading live AI chat) risks this regime, whereas examining stored data after the fact is treated differently (distinction unverified). Article titles verified; text and application to corporate proxies unverified.
bullets.confidence: official-doc for article titles only (law.go.kr page title listing); unverified for application

bullets.topic: Personal Information Protection Act (개인정보 보호법) and monitoring consent
bullets.text: Employee PC/network monitoring involves processing personal information; a law-firm commentary reports courts accept messenger/PC review only with express consent or where the company's legitimate interest clearly outweighs the employee's rights, and only within a limited scope. Specific PIPA articles (e.g. 15, 17) and consent form requirements were searched but not confirmed. Recommend documented policy, notice and written consent in employment rules/onboarding.
bullets.confidence: third-party (law-firm commentary via search summary); unverified (article numbers)

bullets.topic: Digital evidence admissibility: identity and integrity
bullets.text: Korean case law as summarized by practitioners requires that printouts/copies be shown identical to the original storage medium and that integrity was preserved from seizure to output; hash comparison and participation of the data subject are used to prove it, and failure can lead to exclusion. Forensic workflow should record hashes at acquisition. Case numbers not captured this session.
bullets.confidence: third-party (lawtalk and practitioner articles via search summary)

bullets.text: A Supreme Court civil decision 2024다222212 on admissibility of illegally collected evidence in civil litigation exists but its holding was not retrieved; do not rely on it until read. Criminal Procedure Act principles (exclusion of illegally collected evidence) are background knowledge, unverified here.

AI vendor-side records (Compliance API exports, Purview, Workspace logs) are held by tenant admins; obtaining another party's tenant data, or data transferred abroad, raises PIPA overseas-transfer and consent issues and may need admin cooperation or legal process. Retention windows differ (OpenAI Logs Platform 30 days; Purview third-party AI audit 180 days), so preservation requests should be prompt. Korean cross-border transfer rules themselves: unverified.
bullets.confidence: official-doc for retention figures (Purview) / unverified (OpenAI 30 days via summary); unverified for Korean transfer rules
